data.text: A man who hardens his neck after many rebukes will suddenly be broken beyond healing.
data.titulo: Correction and the Public Fruit of Righteousness

data.text: When the righteous increase, the people rejoice, but when a wicked man rules, the people groan.
A man who loves wisdom gladdens his father, but a companion of prostitutes destroys his wealth.
By justice a king establishes a land, but a man who exacts gifts tears it down.
A man who flatters his neighbor spreads a net for his feet.
In an evil man’s transgression there is a snare, but a righteous person sings and rejoices.
A righteous person knows the cause of the poor; a wicked man does not understand such knowledge.
data.titulo: Knowledge, Anger, and Responsibility for Life

data.text: Scoffers inflame a city, but the wise turn away anger.
When a wise man goes to court with a fool, whether there is rage or laughter, there is no rest.
Bloodthirsty men hate a blameless man, but the upright seek to preserve his life.
A fool gives full vent to his spirit, but a wise person holds it back.
If a ruler listens to falsehood, all his servants are wicked.
The poor man and the oppressor meet together; the LORD gives light to the eyes of them both.
A king who judges the poor faithfully will have his throne established forever.
The rod and correction give wisdom, but a child left to himself brings shame to his mother.
data.titulo: Formation and the Reception of God’s Word

data.text: When the wicked increase, transgression increases, but the righteous will see their downfall.
Discipline your son, and he will give you rest; he will give delight to your soul.
Where there is no prophetic vision, the people cast off restraint, but blessed is the one who keeps the law.
A servant is not corrected by words alone; though he understands, he does not respond.
Do you see a man hasty in his words? There is more hope for a fool than for him.
Whoever pampers his servant from youth will have him become a son in the end.
An angry man stirs up strife, and a man of wrath abounds in transgression.
data.titulo: Pride, Complicity, and Trust in the LORD

data.text: A man’s pride will bring him low, but one who is lowly in spirit will obtain honor.
Whoever shares with a thief hates his own life; he hears the oath’s curse but does not tell.
The fear of man brings a snare, but whoever trusts in the LORD will be safe.
Many seek a ruler’s favor, but a man’s justice comes from the LORD.
An unjust man is an abomination to the righteous, and one whose way is upright is an abomination to the wicked.
